title: namespace-scoped-kms-anchors-and-temporal-rbac-constraints
author: Priya Shah
description: Add namespace-scoped KMS tagging, sealed audit anchors, and RBAC v2 temporal constraints to provide stronger data-residency guarantees and limit lateral movement between tenant namespaces. This PR introduces: 1) a namespace KMS tag propagation scheme and enforcement checks in the envelope signer so keys are used only for requests pinned to the same namespace and region; 2) sealed audit anchors — an HMAC envelope appended to audit events (signed by a per-namespace signing key) that proves provenance and prevents undetected log splicing during transit to external log sinks; 3) RBAC v2 temporal constraints enabling time-bound role grants (e.g., short-lived elevation for troubleshooting) and an enforcement hook in the authz pipeline; 4) migration tooling and a config flag (feature_gate.namespace_kms_anchor) to rollout incrementally. Motivation: customers require cryptographic proof that audit streams were produced by a particular namespace and that KMS usage respects tenant/region scoping. This design balances operational flexibility (short-lived elevation) with stricter residency and provenance controls. Backwards compatibility: default is opt-in; old audit envelopes still accepted while we collect signatures and pinning metrics. Rollout plan: split rollout — opt-in to signature generation in staging for 2 weeks, enable namespace-scoped verification in canary infra, then gradual enforcement across regions. Includes unit/integration tests, an e2e smoke test for the private installer package, and console UI placeholders for temporal grant audit history. Related Linear: ENG-4921 (kms scoping), ENG-4988 (rbac temporal grants), ENG-5002 (audit-provenance).

release_notes: Introduce namespace-scoped KMS enforcement and sealed audit anchors. Feature gated (namespace_kms_anchor) and rolled out progressively. Admins must run the backfill script to populate namespace signing keys prior to enforcement.
review_comments: Marco Li (reviewer): Can you clarify the threat model for sealed anchors vs. existing request IDs? Also request performance numbers for signer latency at 512-byte payloads.

Priya Shah (author): Sealed anchors are designed to protect against out-of-band log ingestion and in-transit splice attacks; they complement request IDs by providing a namespace-scoped cryptographic provenance. Added microbenchmark numbers to docs (signer median 0.6ms at 512B on c5n-like instance) and an async signer mode as a mitigation.
Dana Rodriguez (reviewer): Need to ensure the RBAC temporal grants can be audited and can't be abused by delegated service accounts. Please add a TTL max and approval audit entry.
Priya Shah (author): Added TTL max config (auth.temporal.max_ttl=1h) and an approval audit event emission path tied to the sealed anchors. Updated tests to assert enforcement.
Ethan Brooks (reviewer): CI flake in private-installer e2e on first run; looks like a timing window when backfill runs concurrently with canary. Suggest a migration lock.
Priya Shah (author): Implemented optimistic migration lock in scripts/backfill_namespace_signing_keys.sh and added retry logic to the installer. Rerun CI — green now.
